notes: DIG predates beta-blockers, MRAs and SGLT2 inhibitors; DECISION (contemporary background) is much smaller and gets ~7-9% of the weight. source.trial: Cochrane review of diuretics for chronic HF
source.citation: Faris RF, et al. Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2012;(2):CD003838

population: Chronic HF, any EF; placebo-controlled evidence is 169-202 patients, 1980s-90s
quote: Mortality was lower for participants treated with diuretics than for placebo, odds ratio (OR) for death 0.24, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.07 to 0.83; P = 0.02. Admission for worsening heart failure was reduced in those taking diuretics in two trials (169 participants), OR 0.07 (95% CI 0.01 to 0.52; P = 0.01).
extrapolation: No direct randomized evidence of benefit or harm for this outcome in this band; assumed neutral (rr 1.0, null interval) per owner ruling.
notes: EVIDENCE FOR benefit: Cochrane 2012 (14 trials, 525 participants, 7 placebo-controlled): mortality in 3 placebo-controlled trials (202 participants) OR 0.24 (95% CI 0.07-0.83; P=0.02); admission for worsening HF in 2 trials (169 participants) OR 0.07 (0.01-0.52; P=0.01). AGAINST using those numbers: tiny pre-ACE-inhibitor/beta-blocker/MRA/SGLT2i trials, implausibly large effects, and a no-diuretic arm cannot be rerun in congested patients. NO DIFFERENCE between loops: TRANSFORM-HF (torsemide vs furosemide, n=2859): death 373/1431 (26.1%) vs 374/1428 (26.2%), HR 1.02 (0.89-1.18); total hospitalizations rate ratio 0.94 (0.84-1.07); 'Results were similar across prespecified subgroups, including among patients with reduced, mildly reduced, or preserved ejection fraction' (JAMA 2023, PMID 36648467). DOSE (PMID 21366472) compared bolus vs infusion and low vs high dose, not drug vs none. Furoscix/SC furosemide: no outcome trial vs none; SUBCUT-HF II (PMID 42872757) tested an early-discharge strategy (HF readmissions 13 [14%] vs 5 [6%], OR 2.45, 0.81-7.43), not the drug. OWNER DECISION: neutral (1.0) vs Cochrane ORs as a low-credibility meta-analysis row.

source.citation: Trullas JC, et al. Eur Heart J 2023;44:411-21; EF split JACC Heart Fail 2024;12:1719-30 (PMID 38934966)

population: Acute HF inpatients (median LVEF 55%), n=230; no chronic outcome trial
quote: There were no differences in mortality or rehospitalizations.
extrapolation: No direct randomized evidence of benefit or harm for this outcome in this band; assumed neutral (rr 1.0, null interval) per owner ruling.
notes: EVIDENCE: CLOROTIC (230 acute-HF inpatients, median LVEF 55%, 72% LVEF >40%; HCTZ vs placebo added to IV furosemide for 4 days): 'There were no differences in mortality or rehospitalizations'; the EF-split paper: 'no significant differences observed with the addition of HCTZ in terms of mortality, rehospitalizations, or safety endpoints ... among the 2 LVEF groups'. No hazard ratios are in any abstract, so none is entered. HCTZ added weight loss (2.3 vs 1.5 kg) but more renal-function worsening (46.5% vs 17.2%). This is an acute diuretic-response trial, not a chronic outcome trial; metolazone and chlorthalidone have no HF outcome RCT that I found, so CLOROTIC is applied to all three. OWNER DECISION: neutral (1.0).
